title: How Ancient Bones Proved Cancer Is Older Than Humanity — 1.7-Million-Year Swartkrans SK 7923 Osteosarcoma, Amara West, Age-Standardization Math & Micro-CT Marrow Metastases

teenKit.tldr: Cancer isn't a modern invention caused by industrial pollution or Wi-Fi; high-tech scans of a 1.7-million-year-old hominid foot bone prove it's an ancient biological risk built into multicellular life itself.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Shattering the myth that ancient lifestyles protected humans from cancer proves that vulnerability to malignancy is a fundamental feature of biology, helping us view modern medicine and disease with deeper scientific accuracy.
keyTakeaways: Fossilized evidence like the Swartkrans SK 7923 osteosarcoma proves cancer existed millions of years before modern industrial toxins or processed foods.
Advanced tools like micro-CT scans allow scientists to peer inside ancient fossilized bone marrow and map out hidden diseases that are invisible to the naked eye.
Understanding the true history of disease shifts our perspective from blaming modern lifestyle habits to recognizing cancer as an intrinsic flaw in cell division across all multicellular life.

vocab.meaning: The scientific study of ancient diseases preserved in fossils, mummies, and archaeological remains.
An aggressive type of bone cancer that starts in the cells responsible for forming new bone tissue.
A high-resolution 3D imaging technique that uses X-rays to see inside objects down to the microscopic level without destroying them.
A primate of a taxonomic family that includes humans and our extinct bipedal ancestors.

quiz.question: What major modern myth about cancer does the 1.7-million-year-old Swartkrans foot bone completely shatter?
options: That cancer can only be diagnosed using high-tech hospital scanners.
That cancer is an artificial byproduct created solely by modern industrial pollution, smog, and processed foods.
That ancient humans never experienced any type of physical injuries or broken bones.
That cancer is a contagious virus passed between different species of primates.
quiz.explanation: Finding osteosarcoma in a fossil predating industrialization and fire control proves cancer is not exclusively a modern curse.

quiz.question: How were scientists able to detect deep-seated bone cancer inside a fossilized foot bone millions of years old?
options: By carbon-dating the skin cells preserved on the outside of the fossil.
By cutting the fragile fossil completely in half to inspect the inner layers with a magnifying glass.
By using advanced high-resolution micro-CT imaging to peer inside the bone marrow structure.
By matching the bone shape to modern medical textbook diagrams.
quiz.explanation: Micro-CT scans provide a non-destructive way to map the internal architecture and hidden marrow of ancient, stone-turned bones.

quiz.question: According to the episode, what is the truer biological explanation for why cancer occurs?
options: It is a supernatural punishment recorded in ancient Egyptian surgical papyri.
It is a modern mutation triggered exclusively by 21st-century Wi-Fi signals.
It is a fundamental vulnerability intrinsically tied to the mechanics of multicellular life and cell division.
It only occurs in species that have stopped eating raw meat.
quiz.explanation: Malignancy is a baseline biological risk that comes with being a multicellular organism whose cells constantly divide.
